output.summary: Set MAX_REPLICA_COUNT to 8 in perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp and replaced the all-or-nothing cap check with a fallback that halves the replica count until it fits. K=8 made q01 slower in both benches: 280.4 -> 297.7 ms (+6.2%) and 284.9 -> 327.1 ms (+14.8%). Then tried the fallback alone (K=4 with halving). q01's domain fits the cap at K=4, so it runs the same code as best; three benches gave -14.6%, -3.7% and -3.5%, which is noise. No measurable gain on the visible template.
output.generality: The fallback would only help perfect-hash group-bys whose group domain times tuple size is between 256KiB and 1MiB, which today get no replication. No visible template has a domain that size, so the gain cannot be shown here. K=8 is harmful for small skewed domains like q01's.
output.notes: K=8 is a dead end: it is consistently slower than K=4 on q01 (+6% and +15%). Likely causes are more cache footprint or wider address scatter per chunk; dependency chains no longer seem to be the bottleneck after E0005. Note that q01 bench noise is large: a run with identical code showed -14.6%. For PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY, look elsewhere next: computing group location and address in one pass (fusing the ComputeGroupLocation loop with the replica-address loop), or skipping the memset/group_is_set writes. The replica loops (CombineReplicas, the Scan fold, Init, Destroy) all loop over replica_count, with no hard-coded 4.
